title: Garganega
description: Soave's grape: almond, lemon and volcanic minerality, dry or sweet as Recioto.
L: Garganega gives light to medium-bodied whites with lemon, pear, white peach, almond, white flowers and a saline, mineral edge. Acidity is medium to high. It's the main grape of Soave, in the Veneto. With age, it gains honey and nutty notes.

Garganega is one of Italy's oldest white grapes, recorded around Verona since the 13th century. DNA shows it's identical to Sicily's Grecanico and related to many central Italian grapes, like Trebbiano Toscano. It's vigorous and late-ripening; yields must be controlled for quality.
What is Garganega called in Sicily?
DNA shows Garganega and Grecanico are the same grape.

Look for pale lemon colour, lemon and almond, a light floral note, and a crisp, slightly saline palate with a bitter almond finish. Better Soave has more body and texture. Compared with Pinot Grigio, Garganega has more almond and minerality.
Garganega is the main grape of Soave.
Yes. Soave must be at least 70% Garganega.

Explain the role of volcanic soils

Garganega grows mainly in the Veneto, east of Verona, around Soave. Soave DOC must be at least 70% Garganega, with Trebbiano di Soave or Chardonnay. Soave Classico, in the hills around Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, is the historic core. Gambellara, next door, also uses it.

Soave Classico's hills have volcanic basalt soils, dark and mineral-rich, as well as limestone. Volcanic soils give wines with more structure, saline notes and ageing potential. Vineyards are traditionally trained on pergolas, called pergola veronese, which shade the fruit. Flat land below makes simpler Soave.
Soave's hills give its best wines.

Since 2019, Soave recognises 33 Unità Geografiche Aggiuntive, named sub-areas, like Foscarino, Calvarino and Monte Fiorentine. These help consumers find the best sites. Producers like Pieropan and Inama helped show Soave's potential.
What soils give Soave Classico its structure?
Basalt and limestone give mineral, structured wines.
Garganega grows around Soave, east of Verona
Soave Classico's volcanic hills give its best wines

In the 1970s and 1980s, Soave was mass-produced and cheap, giving it a poor reputation. Better producers lowered yields, focused on hillside sites and made more serious wines. Soave Superiore DOCG and Soave Classico Superiore require lower yields and longer ageing. Top Soave can age 10 years or more.

Recioto di Soave, the region's first DOCG in 1998, is a sweet wine from dried Garganega. Grapes are dried for months on racks, appassimento, concentrating sugar, sometimes with noble rot. The wine is golden, honeyed and sweet, with apricot and almond, balanced by acidity.
How is Recioto di Soave made?
Appassimento concentrates sugar in the grapes.
Look for Soave Classico from named sub-areas, such as Foscarino or Calvarino. They often show the volcanic, saline side of Garganega.
Soave moved from cheap volume to serious quality

Soave suits light Italian food: risotto with spring vegetables, seafood, grilled fish, antipasti and fresh cheeses. Its almond notes suit dishes with nuts, and its saline edge suits shellfish. Aged Soave suits richer fish and white meat.

Recioto di Soave suits almond biscuits, pandoro, fruit tarts and blue cheese. Serve Soave at 8 to 10 degrees, Recioto at 10 to 12. Simple Soave is best young; Classico from top sites ages 10 years; Recioto can age decades.
Verona's pandoro, a tall star-shaped cake, and a glass of Recioto di Soave is a local Christmas pairing.
Recioto di Soave can age for decades.
Yes. Its sugar and acidity preserve it.
